source.publication: Jiji Press via nippon.com / BoJ policy statement

description: At its 2026-09-18 meeting the Bank of Japan raised its policy rate 25bp to about 1.25%, the highest in roughly 31 years, by 7-2 (Toichiro Asada and Ayano Sato dissented in favour of holding); the new rate takes effect on 2026-09-24. It is the shortest interval between hikes under Governor Ueda (first hike in three months) and was explained by inflation expected to run clearly above 2% from the second half of fiscal 2026. The move matched forecasts and was received as dovish: with two dissents and no promise of further hikes the yen FELL rather than rose. Registered late: the 2026-10-17 scan triaged it first as below_threshold on a -5 judgement adjustment off a rubric total of 55; the review applied the rubric as written (55 meets the 55 threshold), since the adjustment is exactly the cardinal the rubric exists to remove. The scorer-relevant link is structural: it confirms the BoJ-normalisation leg of struct_japan_carry_unwind; no investable sector is claimed (that structural is listed in no sector study), and the global-yield channel into held sectors is already carried by the Fed and ECB hike events.
